credited.title: Nominal reads may write
credited.credited_stage: compare (Opus 5). The Muse breadth stage credited nothing - see stage_attribution.
credited.basis: The sharpest form of this proposition in the campaign, because it is aimed at the one place the corpus thought it was already safe. JJI-008 AC5 requires verification reads to be 'ignore-working-copy where required' and the schema assertion says such a read 'does not manufacture a JJ snapshot'. The arm shows that covers only half the effect: jj's own CLI reference says 'jj op log snapshots the current working-copy changes AND RECONCILES DIVERGENT OPERATIONS. Use --at-op=@ --ignore-working-copy to inspect the current state without mutation', and '--at-op=@ is pretty much the same as the default except that divergent operations will never be merged'. So a compliant restore drill can capture a two-head store, run an --ignore-working-copy read, silently merge the two heads into an operation that never existed in the source, and still record verified_on_disposable_copy. The repair extends AC5 to 'neither a hidden JJ snapshot NOR a new operation, including operation-head resolution/merge, op-head marker rewriting, or rebuild-on-read of derived state'.
code_fact_verification: V-B1 jj CLI reference (job receipts S00057/S00058, HTTP 200): ':2037 Like other commands, jj op log snapshots the current working-copy changes and reconciles divergent operations. Use --at-op=@ --ignore-working-copy to inspect the current state without mutation' and ':850 --at-op=@ is pretty much the same as the default except that divergent operations will never be merged.' VERIFIED VERBATIM in both receipts.

credited.title: Writer authority is stronger than native locks
credited.credited_stage: compare (Opus 5). The Muse breadth stage credited nothing - see stage_attribution.
credited.basis: Two jobs. J0051 records that the Plans are already stronger than the external comparator here - 'one repository writer (Plans stronger than a per-window worker)' - and J0056 F1 states the gap that remains: 'No foreign-JJ-writer model. The Plans' concurrency invariant is Git-vs-JJ (JJI-004). PM's writer lease is a PM-internal lease and cannot bind a Watchman trigger, a VisualJJ/IDE snapshot, a user's jj CLI, or a second jj git fetch. Upstream states plainly that such writers exist and that jj cannot prevent external Git tools either. No Plans passage anticipates ANOTHER JJ WRITER advancing the operation log during a PM-issued command.' Literal corpus searches for 'Watchman' and 'background snapshot' returned no matches.

credited.title: Expected operation is not native compare-and-swap
credited.credited_stage: compare (Opus 5). The Muse breadth stage credited nothing - see stage_attribution.
credited.basis: GAINED OVER claude-hicap. J0056 F2 states the proposition including its distinctive after-a-long-fetch clause: 'Precondition is checked at request time, never re-checked after the network phase. currentness_fence.expected_operation_id is stamped with checked_at_utc at request; nothing in JJI-003/§3.3 or the schema requires the adapter to re-verify the operation head immediately before the import/ref-update phase of a fetch. This is exactly the window PR 9829 addresses.' It also disposes of the near-fit: SCS-015's 'execution rechecks it' is 'about the capability decision, not the operation fence, and it is a Source Control sentence, not a JJ transport obligation.'

credited.title: Process failure and cancellation are not no-effect proof
credited.credited_stage: compare (Opus 5). The Muse breadth stage credited nothing - see stage_attribution.
credited.basis: Three independent statements. J0048 R3: 'A non-succeeded terminal result must disclose whether a native mutation occurred' - the frozen vocabulary requires a null after-revision only for effect_unknown, so 'failed and cancelled are silent about whether the repository changed', against the verified native behaviour that cmd_resolve rewrites the commit and awaits tx.finish BEFORE returning the partial-resolution error. J0048 R2 adds that a helper's own structured success signal - an HTTP 200 on a save endpoint, a zero exit code, a closed browser tab - is never the command's terminal result. J0053 supplies the cancellation half: cancellation is classified from an adapter-held signal record, never from exit status, and 'a kill sweep is not an effect proof'.

credited.title: Native versus sidecar crash boundary
credited.credited_stage: compare (Opus 5). The Muse breadth stage credited nothing - see stage_attribution.
credited.basis: Three jobs, and the sharpest line in the campaign for this proposition: J0047's 'presence and reachability are not integrity'. It shows a torn pack 'hashes identically on both sides, so a faithful copy of a corrupt store passes every existing check and is still certified complete', and that the corpus's capture-fidelity requirement proves the copy matches the source but not that the source object graph is intact. J0052 adds the recovery half - 'Native recovery is inadmissible in exactly the state that needs it' and 'No recovery path validates' because allowed_action_ids may be empty - and J0057 adds that crash damage is not a distinct recovery state and there is no 'preserve the damaged copy first' rule.

credited.credited_stage: compare (Opus 5). The Muse breadth stage credited nothing - see stage_attribution.
credited.basis: J0052 states it as a disclosure obligation: 'No disclosure of what native JJ recovery does NOT restore.' The arm keeps undo, op restore, workspace path recovery and external-file recovery distinct and requires the contract to say which of them a given recovery route covers, rather than presenting native recovery as a single capability.

credited.title: Change evolution view
credited.credited_stage: compare (Opus 5). The Muse breadth stage credited nothing - see stage_attribution.
credited.basis: GAINED OVER claude-hicap AND Arm P. J0055's L-28f7a36f8557 is the proposition: 'Native change evolution distinguishes rewrites from source ancestry.' The arm establishes that the native model separates a change's evolution (predecessors, rewrites, abandoned versions) from commit ancestry, and that the corpus has no surface that renders the first - so a per-change evolution view is a distinct capability rather than a relabelling of history.

credited.title: Persistent review marks
credited.credited_stage: compare (Opus 5). The Muse breadth stage credited nothing - see stage_attribution.
credited.basis: REACHED BY NO ARM IN THE ENTIRE CAMPAIGN BEFORE THIS ONE. J0054 Proposal P2: 'JJ review marks/notes keyed to content identity, not text similarity' - a review-state layer where a file's or hunk's reviewed state is keyed to the diff's blob-pair identity (old blob id, new blob id, path) plus the JJ revision fence, 'instead of text position/quote matching. Marks survive rebases/amends/squashes that preserve bytes and invalidate exactly the files whose bytes changed; a mark cannot attach to a different change's content because the key IS the content.' The stale-or-orphaned clause is stated as the defect it fixes: the corpus's existing quote matching 'at >=0.97 similarity will happily re-anchor onto a similar region of a divergent change; the existing negative constraint forbids silent DROPPING, not silent MIGRATION.' It is grounded in a shipped precedent rather than speculation: JayJay replaced mtime-keyed marks with blob-ID content identity, including the deleted-file case keyed on the parent's bytes.

credited.title: Included tools and exact qualification
credited.credited_stage: compare (Opus 5). The Muse breadth stage credited nothing - see stage_attribution.
credited.basis: Two instances. J0052: 'Version-compatible is asserted without a typed field. JJI-008 requires restore verification to be version-compatible' with nothing to check it against. J0056 supplies the object-format half with an additive correction the arm verified itself: the hash choice 'is structural inside jj, not only a display format' because GitBackend derives its root commit/tree IDs from repo.object_hash() and switches on object_hash().len_in_bytes(), 'So JJ commit IDs in a SHA-256 repository are 64-hex, not 40-hex.' The arm then shows object format is absent from the JJI-006 §4.2 setup-row inventory, from jujutsu_revision and from the JJ currentness fence, while git_revision requires it.

credited.title: Native conflict truth and supported shape
credited.credited_stage: compare (Opus 5). The Muse breadth stage credited nothing - see stage_attribution.
credited.basis: Five numbered defects, the most complete statement in the campaign. (1) 'no_conflict_markers is an unsound test, and for Jujutsu it is a FORBIDDEN one' against JJI-005's own negative constraint. (2) 'The resolution vocabulary cannot express a jj conflict' - ours|theirs|both against a model with arbitrarily many sides. (3) 'There is no JJ conflict route at all. The 31-command inventory has no conflict command'. (4) 'git_available is the wrong gate' - the corpus's only conflict entrypoint is unreachable in a non-colocated JJ repository. (5) 'Byte fidelity is nowhere represented' - §3.2 promises a conflict-state delta in receipts with no marker-style, side-count or byte requirement behind it.

credited.title: Exact-profile conflict byte regression
credited.credited_stage: compare (Opus 5). The Muse breadth stage credited nothing - see stage_attribution.
credited.basis: GAINED OVER claude-hicap. J0057 names the exact-profile defect from the materialize/parse path rather than from release dating: 'materialization normalizes to a detected LF or CRLF and appends ... each term and then UNCONDITIONALLY pops a following \r. A term whose genuine last byte is a bare \r loses it on roundtrip', with the fix commit's own explanation of the consequence, and an acceptance fixture requiring that 'a term whose original content ends in a bare \r roundtrips through materialize/parse'. The repair also requires the receipt to carry the active marker style, marker_len and detected_eol so the profile's fidelity is disclosed rather than assumed.

credited.title: Push targets and bookmark effects
credited.credited_stage: compare (Opus 5). The Muse breadth stage credited nothing - see stage_attribution.
credited.basis: Two jobs covering both clauses. Preserve the state axes: J0055 Gap 1 is 'state flattening' - every typed bookmark surface in the corpus is a bare name - and Gap 2 is that 'conflicted bookmarks have no representation'. Preview the exact effects: J0050 B.2 is 'Remote scope is lost in results, receipts and confirmation text', and J0055 Gap 3 is that 'delete's remote effect is invisible'. The repair adds a typed bookmark reference, binds conflicted bookmarks before effect, separates the three intents in the contract rather than only in copy, and surfaces remote freshness separately from intent.

Add bookmark_conflicted to both [vocabularies]' so a conflicted bookmark is admitted as a distinct state with its local and remote targets reviewable, rather than being flattened into a bare name and acted on blind.

credited.credited_stage: compare (Opus 5). The Muse breadth stage credited nothing - see stage_attribution.

credited.title: Partial clone and LFS/submodule eligibility
credited.credited_stage: compare (Opus 5). The Muse breadth stage credited nothing - see stage_attribution.
credited.basis: Four numbered gaps, and the never-silently-hydrate clause is the centre of them: 'Nothing detects a filtered/promisor repository'; 'closure_state: complete can be satisfied by objects that are not local'; 'Capture and verification may SILENTLY HYDRATE AND AUTHENTICATE'; and 'No promised-absent vs damaged classification anywhere.' The arm grounds the mechanism in Git's own design document - a failed object lookup invokes the promisor remote and 'For efficiency reasons, no check as to whether the missing object is actually a promisor object is performed' - and notes that unhydrated content 'already has to be marked FOR LFS/SUBMODULES', so the corpus has the shape and applies it to the wrong subset.

credited.title: Operation metadata is not idempotency
credited.credited_stage: compare (Opus 5). The Muse breadth stage credited nothing - see stage_attribution.
credited.basis: J0058's L-2ccd857addc8 is the proposition: native operation attributes can correlate work but are not an idempotency protocol. The arm keeps the durable command-instance identity on PM's side rather than inferring it from native operation metadata, and records that the native attributes are durable user-visible text inside the repository rather than a private correlation channel.

credited.title: Upstream narrative inconsistencies
credited.credited_stage: compare (Opus 5). The Muse breadth stage credited nothing - see stage_attribution.
credited.basis: Sustained, and the flagship instance is a correction of the arm's OWN inherited reconcile. The Muse stage retained Dojjo's comment - 'Do not use --connectivity-only: it skips unreachable refs such as refs/jj/keep/*' - as explicitly unverified. J0047 fetched git-fsck's documentation and resolved it: 'the OPERATIONAL conclusion (use a full fsck) is right, but the stated REASON is wrong: refs - including refs/jj/keep/* - are reachability roots, so --connectivity-only neither skips them nor misses objects that are absent. What it misses is BYTE-LEVEL CORRUPTION inside objects, blobs especially. The transferable rule is "presence and reachability are not integrity", which is stronger and differently scoped than the Dojjo comment. Do not carry the Dojjo wording into PM material. This supersedes the "retained as unverified" status in the J0019 child note.' Eleven of the twelve compare jobs carry comparable correction sections.
